title: Why the after-hours joints closed
summary: Rock changed the audience from spenders to people nursing a beer, so after-hours clubs ended around the 1950s.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: There was always a place to play after-hours in L.A. until what? About the '50s?

I don't know. There was still -- yeah, that's about the time when those -- all of the after-hour joints closed up for some reason. Things started getting different when the rock and that type of music came in. Different people started going out. See, people, they used to go out at after-hour joints were people that came out to spend money and when the rock business came in, that was a different culture altogether. Those were people that sat over a bottle of beer all night long into a place and they didn't want to dance or do anything else. I don't know. The jazz scene suddenly changed completely.
